the way i want to try to do this is:

1. user adds tasks as normal but with some way of indicating frequency of recurrence (if marked "complete," a recurring task gets moved down the list rather than deleted)

title: From “I can’t start” to AI that breaks it down for you
summary:
The most telling line in the whole saga is basically: “follow the inscrutable exhortations of your soul. also break tasks down into smaller steps” — @QiaochuYuan accidentally summarizing the entire ADHD/productivity internet in one tweet. The thread’s core “boundary object” is the same pain point over and over: the *insurmountable task* that isn’t hard, it’s just… too undifferentiated to begin.

It starts way pre-AI: in 2015 @visakanv is begging Trello/Asana for a SMART/GTD “video game” onboarding that doesn’t intimidate you with complexity. Then 2021 hits and @goblinodds is like “fine, I’ll build it”: a hacky Python script that randomly drops *one* to-do onto today’s Google Calendar, so you don’t drown in the list (and later reports it’s helping mainly by removing guilt and memory burden). The peak moment is 2023 when @SarahAMcManus posts Goblin.tools (“click the magic wand, it breaks the task into subtasks”), it goes massively viral, and she credits the creator @chton. Immediately the internet does what it does: people stress-test it with cursed inputs (e.g. @easoncxz turning “find a gf” into an 8-step checklist—“Time to objectify people!”) and @AaronBergman18 uses the “make more passionate” feature to iteratively juice up an insult until it’s Shakespearean hate-mail.

Then the discourse kind of… stops being discourse. By Feb 2024 Goblin.tools is canonized as infrastructure when @QiaochuYuan sticks it in an “ADHD megathread” alongside other frameworks. By 2025 it’s fully mainstreamed and professionalized: @gene_jelly praises routine apps like @FlowSavvyApp for one-tap nested subtasks; @darrenangle calls Claude Code a “full on personal assistant” that organizes markdown kanban boards with calendar/email MCPs (“adhd miracle”); @EyalToledano is shipping Taskmaster updates to parse PRDs into breakdowns; and @kevinkern drops a production-grade prompt to split PRDs into AI-executable batches. Why care: this is the story of a coping mechanism turning into a default UI pattern—task decomposition went from “personal hack for overwhelmed brains” to the baseline way people now expect software (and AI agents) to translate intention into action.
